common_name: Rothschild Orange Azalea (Knap Hill-Exbury Parent of Pathfinder and Fool's Folly)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Rothschild Orange is a Knap Hill-Exbury strain deciduous azalea grown today chiefly through its descendants.

directions: Rothschild Orange is an orange-flowered deciduous azalea of the Knap Hill-Exbury strain developed from Lionel de Rothschild's breeding work at Exbury in Hampshire, England. It survives in cultivation mainly as a breeding parent, having been crossed with Rhododendron austrinum by Dr. Eugene Aromi of Mobile, Alabama to found a line of named Gulf Coast-hardy hybrids, including 'Pathfinder' and 'Fool's Folly'. Like other large Knap Hill-Exbury selections it grows into an upright, multi-stemmed deciduous shrub with big spring trusses. Plant in humus-rich, acidic, evenly moist soil in partial shade, and avoid heavy pruning, since flower buds set on the previous year's growth.

common_name: Tintoretto Azalea (Parent of Frontier Red and Spanish Main)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Tintoretto is a deciduous azalea grown today chiefly through its descendants.

directions: Tintoretto is a deciduous azalea documented today mainly through its role as a breeding parent: Dr. Eugene Aromi of Mobile, Alabama crossed his own 'Forty-niner' with 'Tintoretto' to produce the red-orange 'Frontier Red', and crossed 'Tintoretto' directly with Rhododendron austrinum to produce 'Spanish Main'. Like other large deciduous azaleas in the Aromi breeding pool it forms a vigorous, upright shrub with heavy spring trusses. Plant in humus-rich, acidic, evenly moist, well-drained soil in partial shade, and mulch to protect the shallow root system through summer heat.
sources: Journal of the American Rhododendron Society

common_name: Gann's Legacy Azalea (Aromi Hybrid Parent of Old Rose and Country Cousin)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Gann's Legacy is a named Aromi selection valued chiefly as a parent of further Aromi hybrids.

directions: Gann's Legacy is a named selection from Dr. Eugene Aromi's deciduous azalea breeding program in Mobile, Alabama. It has been used as a parent for further Aromi introductions, including 'Old Rose' and 'Country Cousin'. Like other Aromi hybrids it combines native Gulf South azalea species with Exbury parentage for heat and humidity tolerance on a medium, rounded deciduous shrub. Plant in humus-rich, acidic, evenly moist, well-drained soil in partial shade, and mulch to protect the shallow root system through summer heat.

common_name: Mount Rainier Azalea (Exbury Hybrid Parent of Queen's Ivory)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Mount Rainier is an Exbury-strain deciduous azalea used as Aromi breeding parent stock.

directions: Mount Rainier is an Exbury-strain deciduous azalea grown into an upright shrub reaching roughly 5 feet tall and hardy to well below 0 degrees F. Dr. Eugene Aromi of Mobile, Alabama used it as a breeding parent, crossing it to produce 'Queen's Ivory'. Plant in humus-rich, acidic soil with morning sun and afternoon shade, and avoid heavy pruning, since flower buds set on the previous year's growth.

common_name: Waltzing Widow Bearded Iris (1973 Lura Roach Parent of Witches' Sabbath)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes in late summer to early fall with the top surface exposed to the sun in well-drained soil; Waltzing Widow is a deep violet tall bearded iris grown today chiefly as a historic parent cultivar.

directions: Waltzing Widow is a tall bearded iris in deep violet tones, registered in 1973 by hybridizer Lura Roach and blooming at midseason on 40-inch stalks. It is remembered today mainly as a parent cultivar, crossed by William Maryott to produce the purple-black 'Witches' Sabbath', registered in 1982 and introduced in 1986. Set rhizomes horizontally with the top exposed to sunlight in well-drained soil in full sun, and divide congested clumps every three to four years after bloom to maintain vigor.

common_name: Rubyprince Peach (1997 USDA Scarlet Peach, Parent of EveRes Ruby)

planting.note: Plant bare-root trees in winter while dormant; Rubyprince is a vigorous, self-fertile early peach released in 1997 from the USDA Byron, Georgia breeding program.

directions: Rubyprince is an early-season freestone-leaning, semi-clingstone peach released in 1997 from the USDA's Byron, Georgia breeding program, part of the same naming lineage that later produced Sureprince, Julyprince, and Augustprince. It bears large fruit up to 3 inches across with firm, highly flavored flesh under skin that is 80-90 percent scarlet over yellow, ripening roughly two weeks ahead of Redhaven. The self-fertile tree is vigorous and productive but only moderately resistant to bacterial spot; open-pollinated seedlings of Rubyprince were used by Clemson University's peach breeding program as the seed source behind the disease-tolerant 'EveRes Ruby'. Plant in full sun with good drainage, and thin fruit early since this cultivar sets a heavy crop.
sources: Clemson Cooperative Extension Home & Garden Information Center
USDA Agricultural Research Service Byron, Georgia variety records

common_name: Galaxina Arilbred Iris (Paul Black, Related Line to Dykes Medalist Perry Dyer)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes in late summer to early fall with the top surface exposed to the sun in gritty, sharply drained soil, since arilbred irises are especially prone to rot in heavy or wet ground.

directions: Galaxina is an arilbred iris hybridized by Paul Black and registered in 2015 from a 'Gaudy Is Good' sibling crossed with 'Silent Sentry'. Cool white standards carry a mid-yellow blush and a violet flush above, while the falls are light dusky rose-violet with a bold ruby-red spot covering about two-thirds of the center, set off by a white-based, burnt-orange-tipped beard. It earned an Award of Merit in 2022 and comes from the same Black breeding line that produced 'Perry Dyer', winner of the 2024 American Dykes Medal. Set rhizomes shallowly with the top surface exposed in gritty, sharply drained soil, and divide congested clumps every two to three years after bloom.

common_name: Setsukan Nishiki Sacred Lily (Corrugated Omoto Parent of Wrath of Kan)

planting.note: Plant divisions in rich, well-drained soil in light to deep shade; Setsukan Nishiki is a Japanese Rohdea cultivar grown for its thickly corrugated, variegated evergreen leaves and valued as breeding stock.

directions: Setsukan Nishiki is a Japanese Omoto cultivar of Rohdea japonica, prized by collectors for its heavily corrugated, ridged evergreen leaves variegated with creamy white streaking, in the slow-growing, clump-forming habit typical of choice Rohdea selections. A seedling raised from it was selected for notably better vigor than its corrugated parent and introduced by Plant Delights Nursery as 'Wrath of Kan'. Grow in humus-rich, well-drained soil in light to deep shade, and expect slow, steady increase typical of the most heavily textured Rohdea clones.
sources: Plant Delights Nursery / Juniper Level Botanic Garden

common_name: Appalachian Blues Skullcap (West Virginia Scutellaria Hybrid Selection, PP34,854)
scientific_name: Scutellaria 'Appalachian Blues' (S. ovata x S. serrata)

planting.note: Plant divisions or nursery starts in spring in full sun to shade and average, well-drained soil; Appalachian Blues tolerates dry conditions once established and is attractive to bumblebees.

directions: Appalachian Blues is a naturally occurring hybrid between Scutellaria ovata and S. serrata discovered in the mountains of West Virginia and selected by plantsman Peter Heus, patented as PP34,854. It forms a compact clumping skullcap with serrated, dark-margined foliage and spikes of large, hooded, bicolor purple-and-white flowers that bloom for weeks and draw bumblebees readily. It tolerates both sun and shade and, once established, handles dry soils better than many woodland perennials. North Creek Nurseries also offers the sibling seedling 'Bumblebee Blues', selected from the same wild cross with a taller, more floriferous habit. Grow in average, well-drained soil and divide congested clumps in spring to maintain vigor.

common_name: Forbidden Fruit Hosta (Golden-Orange Tetraploid Parent of Fruit Salad)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or fall into humus-rich, evenly moist soil in shade to part shade; Forbidden Fruit is a tetraploid sport of 'Orange Marmalade' with a golden-orange center and blue-green margins.

directions: Forbidden Fruit is a tetraploid sport of 'Orange Marmalade' with a bold golden-orange to yellow leaf center framed by a wide blue-green margin, a bolder color break than most gold-centered hostas. Lavender flowers rise on scapes above the mounded foliage in summer. It has itself sported further, giving rise to the more subtly two-toned 'Fruit Salad'. Plant divisions in humus-rich, evenly moist soil in shade to part shade and divide congested clumps every few years to maintain vigor and color contrast.

common_name: Passing Storm Begonia (Silvery Pink-Veined Rhizomatous Begonia)

planting.note: Grow year-round as a houseplant in bright, indirect light; Passing Storm is a 1983 rhizomatous begonia whose leaves shift from pink to silvery grey as they age.

directions: Passing Storm is a rhizomatous begonia introduced in 1983, bearing tear-shaped leaves that emerge soft pink and gradually age to a shimmering silvery grey, veined in olive-grey, so that new and older leaves mix for an ever-changing two-tone look across the mound. Small white flowers appear above the foliage as a repeat bloomer. It later gave rise to the sport 'Harmony's Stormy Sunset', which carries a looser, more open habit. Pot in a light, fast-draining, humus-rich mix and grow in bright, indirect light, letting the topsoil dry slightly between waterings, and divide the rhizome at repotting time to produce new plants.
sources: American Begonia Society rhizomatous begonia references

common_name: Tamagawa Ryu Sacred Lily (Japanese Dragon-Ridge Omoto Parent of Tama Hilfiger)

planting.note: Plant divisions in rich, well-drained soil in light to deep shade; Tamagawa Ryu is a Japanese 'dragon' type Rohdea cultivar with raised, ridged leaf centers prized by collectors.

directions: Tamagawa Ryu is a Japanese Omoto cultivar of Rohdea japonica belonging to the 'ryu' or dragon-leaf group, characterized by a raised, ridged central spine running down each leaf. It is grown in Japan chiefly by specialist collectors and is documented in the West mainly as the parent of a sport selected for a narrow creamy-white leaf border and matching white central ridge, introduced by Plant Delights Nursery as 'Tama Hilfiger'. Like other choice Rohdea, it is exceptionally slow to divide, so expect new offsets only every few years. Grow in humus-rich, well-drained soil in light to deep shade as a near-maintenance-free evergreen collector's accent.
sources: Plant Delights Nursery / Juniper Level Botanic Garden

common_name: Glärnisch Hydrangea (Teller Series Parent of Nachtigall, Blaumeise, and Eisvogel)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Glärnisch is a Swiss Teller series lacecap hydrangea grown today chiefly through its descendants.

directions: Glärnisch is a lacecap hydrangea from the Swiss Teller series bred at the Federal Research Institute for Horticulture in Wädenswil, Switzerland, named for a mountain in the canton of Glarus rather than the bird names used for most of the series. It survives in cultivation chiefly as a parent: crossed with 'Möwe', that pairing was combined with a 'Bodensee' x 'Enziandom' cross to produce the later Teller releases 'Nachtigall', 'Blaumeise', and 'Eisvogel'. Grow in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade as with other macrophylla cultivars, pruning only lightly right after bloom since flowers form on old wood.

common_name: Fujinami Satsuki Azalea (Kikoshi x Onyo Japanese Satsuki Cultivar)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; Fujinami is an early-20th-century Japanese Satsuki azalea bred from 'Kikoshi' x 'Onyo'.

directions: Fujinami is a Japanese Satsuki azalea bred from a cross of 'Kikoshi' and 'Onyo', one of many named selections produced during the early-to-mid twentieth century flowering of Satsuki breeding in Japan. Like other Satsuki selections it flowers later in the season than Kurume or Southern Indica azaleas, so prune only right after bloom finishes since next year's buds set soon afterward. Grow in acidic, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade, protecting it from hot afternoon sun that can scorch the foliage.
